purpose: Reviewable facade palette proposal; not applied to map tiles or shaders
palettePrinciple: Keep warm-neutral Southern California light but reduce orange chroma in building bases; separate pale cladding from dark/cool glass instead of flattening everything to beige.
method: Primary material descriptions preferred; typed OSM identity retained. Photo pixels are explicitly tagged observational samples under uncontrolled lighting, never physical albedo. Suggested hex values are art-directed adaptations, not sampled exact real-building values.

buildings.material: Aluminum-framed curtain wall with solar-bronze glazing; aluminum corner panels
buildings.observation: Source is architect performing facade investigation. OSM #11181E correctly signals a dark tower. Preserve near-charcoal bronze family; avoid orange bronze and avoid lifting glazing to pale grey merely because reflections are bright.
buildings.suggestionType: aesthetic adaptation for coordinated stylized palette; not measured physical albedo

photo.lightingObservation: daylight; strong sky/cloud reflections; not an intrinsic glazing colour

pixelSample.method: Median of original decoded sRGB image pixels in manually selected ROI; no white balance or light correction

implementation: Resolve verified building identity before material/color tags and generic fallback.
Separate opaque cladding from glazing for mixed facades; color alone will not fix orange glass response.
Replace universal dark-color lightness floor with material-specific appearance policy.
Normalize facade chroma in a perceptual color space before palette quantization; preserve hue and perceptual lightness where feasible.
Keep existing global lighting, vegetation, roads, and generic palette variety; soften only excessive orange chroma.
Re-export all LODs and compare identical day, sunset, and night cameras; preserve Broad illumination, Wilshire plain spire, and obstruction lights.
